page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, set in lines of varying indent; a running head at the top; a tag "AD" printed at the lower right, outside the text block, and treated as a catchword-like mark, not text.

main_text.p:
Spes, inquieta blanda cupidinis
Nutrix, in orbem vota tetenderat,
Rerumque faustus somniabat
Imperium, male certus augur:

Tu bellicosa dux bone Galliae
Sperare promptam cuncta superbiam
Compescuisti: tu dedisti
Indomito laqueos furori.

Quis vultus illi? quis dolor intimis
Arsit medullis? Spiritus impotens
Cum claustra spectaret Mosellae,
Et iuuenum intrepidam coronam.

Sic unda rupes fauit in obuias,
Ignis caminis claufus inaftuat.
Hircana sic tigris cruento
Dente suas furit in catenas.

Sed nota Marti dextra Bironij,
Murisque virtus impatiens tegi
Ut fulsit, & pulsi procella
Cornipedum tremuere campi.

Cex noctefueta degeneres fera
Vexare caulas in timidum pecus
Fortes, ad aspectum Leonem
In latebras pauida recurrunt:

Sic ille nuper spe insatiabili
Complexus orbem, robora Galliae
Spectare vix ausus, recurrit
Ad solitas male cautus artes.

page.notes: The verse is set in italic with roman names and some words in roman. The original line breaks are preserved within each stanza. Doubtful readings: "Cum claustra spectaret Mosellae" — the word after "spectaret" is partly obscured by a mark, read as "Mosellae" [?]. "Tu dedisti" is read as printed. The "AD" at lower right is a printed mark outside the text block, recorded here rather than transcribed as text. Long s has been normalised to s; ligature and italic forms are kept as legible.
